posts.title: Compare the Monthly Payment
posts.caption: Two homes with similar prices can have very different monthly costs once taxes, insurance, HOA dues, and mortgage insurance are considered.

posts.title: What Makes Up Your Monthly Mortgage Payment?
posts.caption: Your monthly payment can include principal, interest, property taxes, homeowners insurance, and—when applicable—mortgage insurance or HOA dues.

posts.title: Change the Filter
posts.caption: A clean HVAC filter supports airflow and helps your system avoid unnecessary strain.

posts.title: Your First Week Matters
posts.caption: Have the home, photos, pricing, and marketing ready before going live.

posts.title: Days on Market
posts.caption: Days on market describes how long a home has been listed for sale.

posts.title: Commute
posts.caption: Try the drive at the time of day you would actually be making it.

posts.title: Get Preapproved Before You Fall in Love
posts.caption: Know your realistic buying range before touring seriously. A preapproval can help keep the search focused.

posts.title: Down Payment ≠ Total Cash Needed
posts.caption: Plan for more than the down payment. Closing costs, inspections, appraisal, prepaids, moving, and early repairs can all require cash.

posts.title: Caulk Is Cheap
posts.caption: Small gaps around wet areas and exterior openings can allow moisture where it does not belong.

posts.title: Curb Appeal Starts Before the Front Door
posts.caption: Buyers form an impression before they walk inside. Clean the entry, trim landscaping, and make the front door feel intentional.

posts.title: Pending
posts.caption: Pending generally means an offer has been accepted and the transaction is moving toward closing.

posts.title: Noise
posts.caption: Visit the area in the morning, evening, and weekend to understand how it really feels.

posts.title: Look Beyond the Cosmetic Stuff
posts.caption: Paint and flooring are easier to change than location, layout, lot, or major systems.

posts.title: Interest Rate vs. APR
posts.caption: Interest rate is the cost of borrowing. APR is a broader annualized measure that can include certain fees.

posts.title: Know the Shutoff
posts.caption: Find your home’s main water shutoff before you need it.

posts.title: Light Matters More Than People Think
posts.caption: Open blinds, clean windows, replace weak bulbs, and keep lighting consistent before photos and showings.

posts.title: Contingent
posts.caption: Contingent generally means a home is under contract while one or more conditions still need to be satisfied.

posts.title: Walkability
posts.caption: Think about the shops, parks, groceries, coffee, transit, and everyday errands you actually use.

posts.title: Budget Beyond the Down Payment
posts.caption: Plan for closing costs, inspections, moving expenses, and early repairs—not only the down payment.

posts.title: What Are Closing Costs?
posts.caption: Closing costs can include lender fees, title and escrow charges, appraisal, recording fees, and prepaid items.

posts.title: Check Your Gutters
posts.caption: Gutters and downspouts should move water away from the house.

posts.title: Declutter Before You Decorate
posts.caption: Buyers need to see the space, not your stuff. Clear counters, reduce furniture, and simplify shelves.

posts.title: Equity
posts.caption: Home equity is the difference between a home’s value and the debt secured by the property.

posts.title: Future Development
posts.caption: Look beyond what is there today. Planned roads, housing, retail, and construction can change the area over time.

posts.title: Don't Shop at Your Max Approval
posts.caption: Your lender’s maximum is not necessarily your comfortable monthly payment. Leave room for repairs, utilities, savings, and normal life after closing.

posts.title: 20% Down Is Not a Universal Rule
posts.caption: Some loan programs allow less than 20% down. Eligibility and requirements vary by borrower and loan program.

posts.title: Clean the Dryer Vent
posts.caption: Keeping the dryer vent path clear supports performance and reduces lint buildup.

posts.title: Don't Over-Improve Before You Sell
posts.caption: Not every upgrade pays you back. Focus first on repairs, cleanliness, paint, lighting, and presentation.

posts.title: Appraisal
posts.caption: An appraisal is a professional opinion of property value commonly used during the lending process.

posts.title: HOA & Rules
posts.caption: Review HOA dues, restrictions, amenities, and governing documents before buying.
